title: Midterm Challenge: Mind, Body & Scientific Rigor

questions.question: A clinical neuroscientist hypothesizes that a new memory-enhancing drug increases acetylcholine release in the hippocampus. In a double-blind trial, what serves as the Dependent Variable?

options.text: The dosage of the drug versus placebo administered
The participants' scores on subsequent episodic memory retention tests
The age and gender of the laboratory staff
The brand of scanner used

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the measured outcome behavior (memory test scores) hypothesized to be affected by the independent drug manipulation.

questions.question: Scenario: Patient Marcus suffers localized brain damage following a motorcycle accident. He can easily understand everything his doctor says, but his speech is slow, halting, and missing grammar. What specific structure was damaged?

options.text: Broca's Area in the left frontal lobe
Wernicke's Area in the left temporal lobe
The Occipital visual association cortex
The Medulla oblongata

questions.explanation: Non-fluent, telegraphic speech with intact comprehension is classic Broca's motor aphasia.

questions.question: Scenario: A pharmaceutical company advertises a herbal beverage claiming it 'permanently detoxifies your synaptic vesicles without diet changes'. How would an empirical psychologist critique this claim?

options.text: Accept it immediately if a famous celebrity endorses it
Demand peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials and check for falsifiability
Assume correlation equates to causation
Rely strictly on introspection to test it

questions.explanation: Scientific claims require empirical peer review, falsifiable testing, and randomized control groups.

questions.question: Scenario: While exploring a dark alley, a sudden loud clang causes an immediate surge in adrenaline, dilated pupils, and tachycardia. Which branch of the nervous system orchestrated this response?

options.text: Parasympathetic Nervous System
Sympathetic Nervous System
Somatic Sensory division
Central Spinal Cord reflex

questions.explanation: The sympathetic branch activates the physiological fight-or-flight mobilization.

questions.question: Scenario: An experimental neurotoxin selectively inhibits voltage-gated sodium ($Na^+$) channels from opening on neuronal axons. What will happen to exposed neurons?

options.text: They will generate constant continuous action potentials
They will be unable to depolarize and cannot fire action potentials
Their myelin sheath will immediately double in thickness
They will convert into glial cells

questions.explanation: Without sodium influx, the neuronal membrane cannot depolarize past threshold to initiate an action potential.

questions.question: Scenario: A split-brain patient is presented with the word 'RING' to their left visual field and 'KEY' to their right visual field. When asked what they saw, what will the patient verbalize?

options.text: 'RING'
'KEY'
'RING-KEY'
They will be unable to speak at all

questions.explanation: The right visual field sends information to the left hemisphere, where vocal speech centers reside, so the patient verbalizes 'KEY'.
